neighbours.label: Names of foods or dishes as the topic noun at the end of a phrase in plain prose (the census signal); the card's top examples are a mixed bag (code identifiers like browser/file, sentence-final periods, 'family', 'construction'), so this covers only part of the pole
fire: After the long hike, my brother and I could only talk about lasagna for the rest of the evening.
The whole article was mostly about sourdough and why it rises so well in cold kitchens.
Our grandmother never wrote anything down, but everyone still remembers her cabbage rolls.
At the market she bought a bag of lentils, a wedge of cheddar, and two ripe mangoes.
He swore that the best thing he ever ate on the trip was a simple bowl of ramen.
The teacher asked the class to write a paragraph describing their favorite kind of pancakes.
There was a long debate in the group chat over whether pineapple belongs on pizza.
Late at night she finally admitted that all she wanted was a plate of fried chicken.
quiet: After the long hike, my brother and I could only talk about the broken tent for the rest of the evening.
The whole article was mostly about skillets and why they hold heat so well in cold kitchens.
Our grandmother never wrote anything down, but everyone still remembers her old wooden spoon.
At the market she bought a ceramic bowl, a canvas apron, and two sturdy baskets.
He swore that the best thing he ever bought on the trip was a simple pocket knife.
The teacher asked the class to write a paragraph describing their favorite kind of bicycles.
There was a long debate in the group chat over whether the restaurant should move downtown.
Late at night she finally admitted that all she wanted was a quiet room at the lake.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Only evidence for a coherent concept is the census (51% of foods vs 0% of everyday objects); the card top examples and band samples are heterogeneous (code names, sentence-final punctuation, abstract nouns), so food is at best a partial label. Near misses use kitchen-adjacent objects and other items in the same frames.
